actualModuleReview.name: BA English: Mentoring Sessions
actualModuleReview.contribution: Mandatory mentoring: eight first-semester and four second-semester sessions; study methods, integrity, feedback and career orientation. Zero credits, not a credit-bearing module.
actualAdmissionText: The mentoring sessions are a compulsory part of the first year (*propaedeuse*) in the BA English Language and Culture.

actualModuleReview.name: English Language 1: The Spoken Word
actualModuleReview.contribution: Pronunciation, phonological control, world accents, lexicology and vocabulary; short research presentations and spoken practice.
actualAdmissionText:
Students other than from the BA English language and culture cannot take this course.

For this course transitional provisions apply. If you are a student who started the BA programme in 2024-2025 or earlier and have to retake this course, please check the ['More info'-tab](https://studiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/studies/BA-ENG?&tab=Meer%20informatie) or contact your [study adviser](mailto:stuco-ba-english@hum.leidenuniv.nl).

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 1: Introduction to Middle English Language and Literature
actualModuleReview.contribution: Chaucer in original Middle English, translation, elementary grammar and medieval cultural history.
actualAdmissionText: A knowledge of English grammar or grammar in another West-European language is recommended for this course.

actualModuleReview.name: Intercultural Literary Legacies: Italian and English Exchanges
actualModuleReview.contribution: English–Italian intertextual/intercultural exchange across literary forms, myth, classical/Biblical legacies, philosophy and modern media.
actualAdmissionText: Students in the BA English Language and Culture, the BA Italian Language and Culture, the minor *De Middeleeuwen en vroegmoderne tijd*, the pre-master Literary Studies and pre-master Linguistics (Modern Languages) have priority to take this course if the course is part of their curriculum. Students who would like to take this course as an elective can be admitted to this course if places are available.

actualModuleReview.name: Introduction to Linguistics
actualModuleReview.contribution: Core phonetics/phonology/morphology/syntax/semantics/pragmatics; introductory psycholinguistics, acquisition, change and regional/social variation.
actualAdmissionText: There are no additional admission requirements.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 1: Introduction to Literary Studies in English
actualModuleReview.contribution: Ten-credit prose, poetry, drama and film criticism; close reading, scansion, narratology, research and contextual analytical writing.
actualAdmissionText: High school diploma equivalent to Dutch VWO level.

actualModuleReview.name: English Language 2: From Scratch to Print
actualModuleReview.contribution: Academic and professional writing, source evaluation, referencing, genre/audience conventions and intercultural politeness.
actualAdmissionText:
Students other than from the BA English language and culture cannot take this course.

For this course transitional provisions apply. If you are a student who started the BA programme in 2024-2025 or earlier and have to retake this course, please check the ['More info'-tab](https://studiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/studies/BA-ENG?&tab=Meer%20informatie) or contact your [study adviser](mailto:stuco-ba-english@hum.leidenuniv.nl).

actualModuleReview.name: Linguistics 2: Describing English Sounds and Sentences
actualModuleReview.contribution: Ten-credit IPA sound production/classification and English constituent/verb-phrase syntax. Current prior-study recommendation uses Intro Linguistics or previous Linguistics1.
actualAdmissionText:
We strongly recommend that you have passed Linguistics 1 in 2025/26 or the Introduction to Linguistics in semester 1 prior to enrolling in this course.

For this course transitional provisions apply. If you are a student who started the BA programme in 2024-2025 or earlier and have to retake this course, please check the ['More info'-tab](https://studiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/studies/BA-ENG?&tab=Meer%20informatie) or contact your [study adviser](mailto:stuco-ba-english@hum.leidenuniv.nl).

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 2: English Literature, ca. 1550 - 1700
actualModuleReview.contribution: Early modern British prose, drama and poetry, sonnet/epic and cultural-historical literary analysis with MLA essay.
actualAdmissionText: Not applicable.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 2: Introduction to Old English Language and Literature
actualModuleReview.contribution: Ten-credit Old English phonology/morphology/syntax, prose/poetry translation, riddles, saints, Beowulf and Anglo-Saxon contexts.
actualAdmissionText: Not applicable.

actualModuleReview.name: Core Curriculum: Humanities in a Digital World
actualModuleReview.contribution: Digital-humanities Media/AI/Data blocks with practical tool assignments and a portfolio; not a full computer-science programme.
actualAdmissionText: This course is open for all students of the Faculty of Humanities.

actualModuleReview.name: English Language 3: Rhetorical Grammar
actualModuleReview.contribution: Grammar, punctuation, collocation and lexicogrammar as stylistic/register tools; accuracy, writing and explanation of rhetorical choices.
actualAdmissionText: Not applicable.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 3: History of the English Language
actualModuleReview.contribution: Historical development of English, standardisation/contact/world varieties; Oxford English Dictionary analysis of formal/semantic change.
actualAdmissionText: It is strongly recommended that you have passed Philology 1 or Philology 2 (or equivalent) prior to taking this course.

actualModuleReview.name: Linguistics 3: Analysing English Syllables and Sentences
actualModuleReview.contribution: Ten-credit phrase/clause argumentation and tree diagrams; English segment/syllable variation, social/regional differences, phonetic transcription and PRAAT.
actualAdmissionText:
We strongly recommend that you have passed Linguistics 2 prior to enrolling in this course.

For this course transitional provisions apply. If you are a student who started the BA programme in 2024-2025 or earlier and have to retake this course, please check the ['More info'-tab](https://studiegids.universiteitleiden.nl/studies/BA-ENG?&tab=Meer%20informatie) or contact your [study adviser](mailto:stuco-ba-english@hum.leidenuniv.nl).

actualModuleReview.name: Core Curriculum: Philosophy of Science
actualModuleReview.contribution: Philosophy of science and humanities methods through Popper, Kuhn, Foucault and modern conceptual frameworks.
actualAdmissionText: No special admission requirements.

actualModuleReview.name: Contemporary Concerns in Film and Literature
actualModuleReview.contribution: Literature, film and media responses to climate, fascism, migration, precarity, heritage and AI. Specific topical cases may change annually.
actualAdmissionText: Not applicable

actualModuleReview.name: English Language 4: Dimensions of Written Text
actualModuleReview.contribution: Register/genre/style and situational writing; explicit human versus AI text questions, group register research and multimodal reporting.
actualAdmissionText: A pass for an introductory course on academic writing and an introductory course on grammar are strongly recommended.

actualModuleReview.name: Linguistics 4: English Phonology and Syntax
actualModuleReview.contribution: Generative English syntax, X-bar, theta roles/Case and movement; suprasegmental phonology, word stress, rhythm and intonation.
actualAdmissionText: We strongly recommend that you have passed Linguistics 2 prior to enrolling in this course.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 3B: British Literature in the Long Eighteenth Century
actualModuleReview.contribution: Selected first-listed British18th-century option: novel formation, slavery/revolution/class/gender, public sphere, Gothic/Romanticism.
actualAdmissionText:
It is strongly recommended that you have passed at least an introductory literary studies course prior to enrolling for this course.

**Please note the following**:

* Student from the BA English Language and Culture and pre-master Literary Studies have priority to take this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective can be admitted to this course if places are available.
* Students from the BA English Language and Culture who take or are planning to take the minor American Studies need to keep in mind that they need to take both Literature 3 courses: Literature *3B* as part of the bachelor programme and Literature *3A* as part of the minor programme.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 3A: American Literature, Beginnings to 1865
actualModuleReview.contribution: Unselected independent American option: early contact to1865, race/gender/freedom/democracy, multilingual colonial canon and its reception.
actualAdmissionText:
It is recommended that you have passed at least an introductory literary studies course prior to enrolling for this course. There are no recommended requirements for minor students American Studies.

**Please note the following**:

* Student from the BA English Language and Culture, minor American Studies and pre-master Literary Studies have priority to take this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective can be admitted to this course if places are available.
* Students from the BA English Language and Culture who take or are planning to take the minor American Studies need to keep in mind that they need to take both Literature 3 courses: Literature *3B* as part of the bachelor programme and Literature *3A* as part of the minor programme.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 4B: British Literature in the Long Nineteenth Century
actualModuleReview.contribution: Selected independent British19th-century prose from Austen to Conrad; Gothic, women, class, empire, science and modernity.
actualAdmissionText:
It is strongly recommended that you have passed at least an introductory literary studies course prior to enrolling for this course.

**Please note the following**:

* Student from the BA English Language and Culture and pre-master Literary Studies have priority to take this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective can be admitted to this course if places are available.
* Students from the BA English Language and Culture who take or are planning to take the minor American Studies (Track II: American Literature and Culture) need to keep in mind that they need to take both Literature 4 courses: Literature *4B* as part of the bachelor programme and Literature *4A* as part of the minor programme.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 4A: American Literature, 1865-1917
actualModuleReview.contribution: Unselected American1865–1917 option: immigration, emancipation, urban/industrial/consumer culture, mass media and diverse literary voices.
actualAdmissionText:
It is recommended that you have passed at least an introductory literary studies course prior to enrolling for this course. There are no recommended requirements for minor students American Studies.

**Please note the following**:

* Student from the BA English Language and Culture, minor American Studies and pre-master Literary Studies have priority to take this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective can be admitted to this course if places are available.
* Students from the BA English Language and Culture who take or are planning to take the minor American Studies (Track II: American Literature and Culture) need to keep in mind that they need to take both Literature 4 courses: Literature *4B* as part of the bachelor programme and Literature *4A* as part of the minor programme.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 4B: Early Modern Everyday English
actualModuleReview.contribution: Selected first-listed Philology option: everyday Early Modern texts, historical sociolinguistics, manuscript transcription and corpus analysis of change.
actualAdmissionText: It is strongly recommended that you have passed Philology 3 (or equivalent) prior to taking this course.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 4A: Highlights of Medieval English Literature
actualModuleReview.contribution: Unselected medieval alternative: Old/Middle English texts, digital humanities, library collections and research essay; translation skills expected.
actualAdmissionText:
During this course, students are expected to be able to translate short passages in Old and Middle English into Modern English. Therefore, it is recommended that students complete Philology 1 (Middle English) and Philology 2 (Old English) before taking this course. Alternatively, prospective students can contact the staff two weeks before the start of the course to get recommendations for online preparatory material.

**Please note**: Student from the BA English Language and Culture and pre-master Literary Studies have priority to take this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective can be admitted to this course if places are available.

actualModuleReview.name: Language Acquisition 5: Theories and Research Methods in Applied Linguistics
actualModuleReview.contribution: Outgoing5-credit applied-linguistics qualitative/quantitative research into identity and language use; last offered2026–2027, excluded from entrant reconstruction.
actualAdmissionText: Not applicable.

actualModuleReview.name: Language Acquisition 6: Language Learning and Teaching
actualModuleReview.contribution: Outgoing5-credit language learning/teaching theory and didactics; last offered2026–2027, excluded from entrant reconstruction.
actualAdmissionText: Not applicable.

actualModuleReview.name: Linguistics 5A: English Sounds and Words in the Mental Lexicon
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit elective mental lexicon, infancy/ageing/second-language effects. Requires old Linguistics3(B); not certified as future entrant replacement.
actualAdmissionText: Students have taken and passed the BA-course Linguistics 3(B). It is strongly recommended to have passed Linguistics 2(A).

actualModuleReview.name: Linguistics 6A: Exploring Change in the History of English: Sounds
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit elective historical sound/word/meaning change, Grimm/Great Vowel Shift and ongoing English variation. Old-code entry condition remains.
actualAdmissionText:
Students need to have passed Linguistics 3(B).
It is strongly recommended to have passed Linguistics 2(A) or another introductory course in linguistics.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 5B: Modern(ist) and Contemporary Literatures in English
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit modern/contemporary English literatures1915–2025 and cultural forces, mainly UK/Ireland with global migration. Future cohort membership unconfirmed.
actualAdmissionText:
Students need to have passed 10 EC in (English) Literature courses. This requirement does not apply to pre-master students Literary Studies.

**Please note:** Students of the BA English Language and Culture and pre-master students Literary Studies have priority in taking this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective and meet the requirements can be admitted to this course if places are available.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 5A: American Literature, 1917 to the present
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit American1917–present modernism/postmodernism, race/gender/feminism, graphic novels and trauma. Future cohort membership unconfirmed.
actualAdmissionText:
Students need to have passed 10 EC in (English) Literature courses. This requirement does not apply to pre-master students Literary Studies and North-American studies.

**Please note:** Students of the BA English Language and Culture and pre-master students Literary Studies have priority in taking this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective and meet the requirements can be admitted to this course if places are available.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 5D: Introduction to American Film
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit American film and cultural history, performance media and genre. Future cohort membership unconfirmed.
actualAdmissionText:
Students need to have passed 10 EC in (English) Literature courses.

**Please note:** Students of the BA English Language and Culture have priority in taking this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective and meet the requirements can be admitted to this course if places are available.

actualModuleReview.name: Literature 6: Shakespeare and Memory
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit Shakespeare/memory across drama and poetry, textual versions and modern scholarly approaches. Future cohort membership unconfirmed.
actualAdmissionText:
Students need to have passed 10 EC in (English) Literature courses.

**Please note:** Students of the BA English Language and Culture have priority in taking this course. Students who would like to take this course as an elective and meet the requirements can be admitted to this course if places are available.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 5B: Unlocking Late Modern English Identities
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit Late Modern English identity, letters/manuscripts, social class/gender and regional/colonial variation. Requires Philology3 or equivalent.
actualAdmissionText: Successful completion of Philology 3 or equivalent.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 5A: Old English Literature and Culture
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit Old English originals, translation, early medieval culture and later reception; original materials/digital techniques.
actualAdmissionText: Completion of Philology 2 or comparable course.

actualModuleReview.name: Philology 6: Middle English Literature and Culture
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit Middle English literature1100–1500 with original-text/glossed analysis and digital web writing.
actualAdmissionText: Successful completion of Philology 1 (Middle English) or a comparable course.

actualModuleReview.name: BA Thesis English Language and Culture
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current10-credit thesis7500–10000 words, two topic proposals from different academic areas and second reader. OER earned130EC controls over module “near future” wording.
actualAdmissionText: Students write their bachelor’s thesis in the last semester of the degree programme. Full-time students must have earned 130 EC or will do so in the near future. Part-time students must already have earned 140 EC. Attending the thesis seminar is mandatory.

actualModuleReview.name: Thesis Seminar BA English Language and Culture
actualModuleReview.contribution: Mandatory thesis work/support seminar; zero credits and no independent thesis credit.
actualAdmissionText: Following the thesis seminar is obligatory when you are writing your BA thesis.

actualModuleReview.name: Elective Space Bachelor 15 EC
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current15EC open-space block; minor, internship, abroad or approved individual package. Genuine open content, no named filler invented.
actualAdmissionText: In terms of academic level, the elective space is best suited to third-year Bachelor’s students who have completed the first year of their Bachelor’s degree.

actualModuleReview.name: Elective Space Bachelor 15 EC
actualModuleReview.contribution: Current second15EC open-space block. Planned block-minor reform is not proof of revised course allocation.
actualAdmissionText: In terms of academic level, the elective space is best suited to third-year Bachelor’s students who have completed the first year of their Bachelor’s degree.

findings: Four interconnected academic fields, not four formal registered specialisations (2.2 not applicable).
C2 reading/listening andC1 speaking/writing aims; Old/Middle English originals and structural/historical linguistic inquiry are defining substance.

Article4.2 sets earned130 programme EC for thesis entry; programme module near-future130 does not override adopted regulation. Other old-code BA3 entries must use actual equivalences, not assumed code equality.
AppendixF has first/second-year substitutions only. No revised BA3 allocation. All written exams/final thesis in English.
formalReview.transitionReconciliation: Appendix F2025 replaces Linguistics3A5EC+3B5EC with combined Linguistics3:Analysing English Syllables and Sentences10EC. This supplies the documented current equivalence for old-codeBA3 prerequisites; it does not establish future module membership or replacement language courses. AppendixF2026 similarly documents the actual first120 substitutions. No false hard prerequisite is created from an advisory recommendation.

publicFindings.finding: Exact full-time3-year English-taught BA in Leiden; distinguish part-time target.
Four learning pathways; authors, historical English originals/manuscripts/digital corpora and explicit human-AI writing analysis. Public examples are not all formal cohort allocations.

Public course examples support phonetics, Old English riddles/heroic/saints, AI-writing comparisons, early American race/freedom and language history; thesis7500–10000words. Public Linguistics2 label differs from current adopted code/name; actual current module controls the partial reconstruction.
Current thesis10EC, seminar0EC, two topic proposals, one-semester process and second-reader assessment; current2026–2027 deadlines cannot establish2028–2029 entry allocation.
Career survey sectors and individual workplaces describe possibilities, not guaranteed qualifications.
Teaching needs a teaching master; combined educational master needs Dutch. Translation further study has conditions in current guide. No UCR admission claim.
